metadata.title: Justin Watson - Back with practice squad
metadata.description: Watson reverted to the Chiefs' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
metadata.analysis: Watson was elevated to the active roster for a second week in a row ahead of Sunday night's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. The wide receiver reeled in his only target for seven yards while playing five snaps on offense and two snaps with the special-teams unit. The Chiefs can elevate Watson one more time before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

metadata.title: Justin Watson - Elevated for Sunday night
metadata.description: The Chiefs elevated Watson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Watson is set for consecutive elevations after participating in the Chiefs' Week 6 win over the Chargers. The wide receiver played just one offensive snap in the contest and will likely be treated as a reserve option once again in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

metadata.title: Justin Watson - Reverts to practice squad
metadata.description: Watson reverted to Kansas City's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction report.
metadata.analysis: Watson was elevated for the first time since returning to the Chiefs but ended up playing just one snap on offense and three on special teams, failing to produce any output in the box score. He could be a candidate to play again in next week's matchup against the Seahawks should Rashee Rice remain sidelined due to a hamstring injury.

metadata.title: Justin Watson - Elevated for Week 6
metadata.description: The Chiefs elevated Watson from the practice squad Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Watson signed with Kansas City earlier this week and will provide the team with experience at wide receiver after Rashee Rice (hamstring) was ruled out for Week 6. Tyquan Thornton (ankle) was also lost to injured reserve two weeks ago.

metadata.title: Justin Watson signs with Chiefs practice squad
metadata.description: The Chiefs signed WR Justin Watson to their practice squad
metadata.analysis: Watson will add depth in the wide receiver room for Kansas City. He remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Justin Watson - Inks practice-squad deal with Kansas City
metadata.description: The Chiefs signed Watson to the practice squad Monday, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Watson failed to make the Texans' 53-man roster at the end of training camp, but he'll get another opportunity with the Chiefs on the practice squad. The veteran wide receiver played three seasons in Kansas City from 2022 to 2024, and in that span, he caught 64 passes on 119 targets for 1,064 yards and seven touchdowns across 50 regular-season games (20 starts). Watson would be a top candidate for elevation to the Chiefs' active roster if Rashee Rice (hamstring) is not cleared to play against the Chargers on Sunday.

metadata.title: Justin Watson released by Texans
metadata.description: The Texans released WR Justin Watson.
metadata.analysis: Watson will seek a depth role with another team on special teams.

metadata.title: Justin Watson - Fails to make Houston's roster
metadata.description: Watson was released by the Texans on Sunday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
metadata.analysis: Watson was in camp with the Texans after appearing in three regular-season games with Houston in 2025. The 30-year-old wide receiver is a veteran of 93 NFL games, so he may garner some interest as a depth option for a team in search of help in the passing game.

metadata.title: Justin Watson - In helmet for minicamp
metadata.description: Watson (concussion) participated during the Texans' minicamp Tuesday, David J. Phillip of the Associated Press reports.
metadata.analysis: Watson suffered a postseason-ending concussion during Houston's wild-card win at Pittsburgh in January, but he's now back to full health with minicamp underway. He currently projects for a depth role in a wide receiver corps led by two-time Pro Bowler Nico Collins and 2025 second-rounder Jayden Higgins.

metadata.title: Justin Watson - Season derailed by calf issue
metadata.description: Watson recorded three receptions for 30 yards on four targets over three regular-season games.
metadata.analysis: Watson, who also suffered a postseason-ending concussion in the wild-card win over the Steelers, logged 40 percent or more of the offensive snaps in Week 1 and Week 2 before succumbing to a calf injury that landed him on injured reserve until the Week 18 matchup against the Colts. The wide receiver only logged 19 percent of the offensive snaps and wasn't targeted in his return. Rookie Jaylin Noel seems to have absorbed Watson's role in the offense, and it is unclear if the veteran will be able to reclaim his role heading into the 2026 season.
